title: Interstate banking deregulation on credit supply

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

This is a classic DID setting: states deregulate interstate banking at period 4 (treated group), while other states remain regulated (control group). We compare the change in log loans-to-assets ratio before vs. after deregulation across treated and control states.

**Key identifying assumption:** Parallel trends — absent deregulation, treated and control states would have followed the same trajectory in log loans-to-assets ratios. We validate this with an event-study specification checking for differential pre-trends.

**Specification:**
- **Main DID:** $y_{it} = \alpha_i + \lambda_t + \beta \cdot \text{treat\_x\_post}_{it} + \varepsilon_{it}$, where $\beta$ is the ATT.
- **Event study:** Replace the single interaction with period-specific interactions (relative to period 3, the last pre-treatment period) to test parallel trends and trace out dynamic treatment effects.
- **Robustness:** Cluster standard errors at the unit level, test sensitivity to excluding periods, and estimate without fixed effects.

## 2. R Code

```r
# =============================================================================
# Interstate Banking Deregulation & Credit Supply — DID Analysis
# =============================================================================

library(fixest)    # For efficient panel estimation with clustered SEs
library(data.table)

# ── Read data ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s05_data.csv")

cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
cat("Observations:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Units:", uniqueN(df$unit_id), "\n")
cat("Periods:", sort(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Treated units:", uniqueN(df[treated==1]$unit_id), "\n")
cat("Control units:", uniqueN(df[treated==0]$unit_id), "\n\n")

# Summary statistics by group and time
cat("=== Mean of y by Group and Pre/Post ===\n")
print(df[, .(mean_y = mean(y), sd_y = sd(y), n = .N), 
         by = .(treated, post)][order(treated, post)])
cat("\n")

# ── Main DID Regression (TWFE) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two-way fixed effects: unit + period FE, clustered SEs at unit level
did_twfe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                  data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("=== Main DID Result (TWFE with unit + period FE) ===\n")
summary(did_twfe)
cat("\nATT estimate:", round(coef(did_twfe)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n\n")

# ── Simple DID (no fixed effects, for comparison) ───────────────────────────
did_simple <- feols(y ~ treated * post, data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)
cat("=== Simple DID (no FE) ===\n")
summary(did_simple)
cat("\n")

# ── Event Study Specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Create relative time variable (event time = period - 4 for treated; 
# for controls, there's no event, so we assign relative time for interactions)
df[, rel_time := period - 4]

# Create event-study dummies: treated × 1(rel_time == k), omitting k = -1
df[, rel_time_factor := factor(rel_time)]

# Event study with TWFE
es_model <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period,
                  data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("=== Event Study Estimates ===\n")
summary(es_model)
cat("\n")

# Plot event study
cat("=== Event Study Coefficients ===\n")
es_coefs <- coef(es_model)
es_se <- se(es_model)
es_table <- data.table(
  rel_time = as.integer(gsub("rel_time::", "", gsub(":treated", "", names(es_coefs)))),
  estimate = es_coefs,
  se = es_se
)
es_table[, `:=`(ci_lo = estimate - 1.96*se, ci_hi = estimate + 1.96*se)]
es_table <- es_table[order(rel_time)]
print(es_table)
cat("\n")

# Check pre-trends: joint test of pre-treatment coefficients
pre_coefs <- grep("rel_time::-[2-9]|rel_time::-[1-9][0-9]", names(coef(es_model)), value = TRUE)
if (length(pre_coefs) > 0) {
  pre_test <- wald(es_model, keep = pre_coefs)
  cat("=== Joint Test of Pre-Trends (H0: all pre-treatment coeffs = 0) ===\n")
  print(pre_test)
  cat("\n")
}

# ── Plot Event Study ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
try({
  pdf("experiments/exp_b/data/event_study_plot.pdf", width = 8, height = 5)
  iplot(es_model, 
        xlab = "Periods Relative to Deregulation",
        ylab = "Effect on Log Loans-to-Assets",
        main = "Event Study: Interstate Banking Deregulation",
        col = "steelblue", ci_col = "steelblue")
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray40")
  abline(v = -0.5, lty = 3, col = "red")
  dev.off()
  cat("Event study plot saved.\n\n")
}, silent = TRUE)

# ── Robustness Check 1: Varying controls ────────────────────────────────────
# Unit FE only (no period FE)
rob1 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id, data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)
cat("=== Robustness: Unit FE Only ===\n")
cat("ATT:", round(coef(rob1)["treat_x_post"], 4), 
    " SE:", round(se(rob1)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n\n")

# Period FE only (no unit FE)
rob2 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post + treated | period, data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)
cat("=== Robustness: Period FE Only ===\n")
cat("ATT:", round(coef(rob2)["treat_x_post"], 4), 
    " SE:", round(se(rob2)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n\n")

# ── Robustness Check 2: Exclude period right around treatment ───────────────
rob3 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
              data = df[period != 4], cluster = ~unit_id)
cat("=== Robustness: Exclude Period 4 (transition period) ===\n")
cat("ATT:", round(coef(rob3)["treat_x_post"], 4), 
    " SE:", round(se(rob3)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n\n")

# ── Robustness Check 3: Placebo test — fake treatment at period 2 ───────────
df_pre <- df[period <= 3]
df_pre[, placebo_post := as.integer(period >= 2)]
df_pre[, placebo_did := treated * placebo_post]

placebo <- feols(y ~ placebo_did | unit_id + period, 
                 data = df_pre, cluster = ~unit_id)
cat("=== Placebo Test: Fake Treatment at Period 2 (pre-treatment data only) ===\n")
summary(placebo)
cat("\n")

# ── Summary Table ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("           SUMMARY OF RESULTS\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Main TWFE DID estimate:    %.4f (SE: %.4f, p: %.4f)\n", 
            coef(did_twfe)["treat_x_post"], 
            se(did_twfe)["treat_x_post"],
            pvalue(did_twfe)["treat_x_post"]))
cat(sprintf("Simple DID estimate:       %.4f\n", 
            coef(did_simple)["treated:post"]))
cat(sprintf("Unit FE only:              %.4f\n", 
            coef(rob1)["treat_x_post"]))
cat(sprintf("Excl. period 4:            %.4f\n", 
            coef(rob3)["treat_x_post"]))
cat(sprintf("Placebo (fake t=2):        %.4f (p: %.4f)\n", 
            coef(placebo)["placebo_did"],
            pvalue(placebo)["placebo_did"]))
cat("============================================================\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Sign:** Positive. Interstate banking deregulation removed barriers to entry, increased competition for deposits, and allowed banks to expand lending across state lines. The literature (Jayaratne & Strahan, 1996; Rice & Strahan, 2010) consistently finds that deregulation increased credit supply.

**Magnitude:** I expect the ATT coefficient on `treat_x_post` to be positive and statistically significant, likely in the range of **0.2–0.5** in log points (corresponding to roughly a 20–65% increase in the loans-to-assets ratio). Given this is simulated data with a clean design, the effect may be sharply estimated.

**Event study:** Pre-treatment coefficients (periods -3, -2 relative to treatment) should be close to zero and statistically insignificant, validating the parallel trends assumption. Post-treatment coefficients should show a clear jump at period 4 and potentially grow over time if the effect is dynamic.

**Placebo test:** The placebo DID coefficient (fake treatment at period 2 using only pre-treatment data) should be small and insignificant, further supporting the identification strategy.

**Robustness:** Results should be stable across specifications (with/without FE, excluding transition period), reinforcing the causal interpretation that deregulation expanded credit supply.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=deregulated states, control=still-regulated; shock=deregulation date
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Credit supply increases significantly after deregulation
